summary: Backend-only verification of the HOD-retest / psych-level / topping-tail auto-trader strategy overhaul in auto_trader_service.py. Created /app/backend/tests/test_hod_psych_topping_tail_strategy.py (6 tests) covering: GET /api/auto-trader/status new strategy fields, POST /api/auto-trader/settings round-trip for enable_partial_profit/breakeven_buffer_pct/topping_tail_wick_ratio (all restored to original values), entry-conditions smoke test for scanner symbols, and a real toggle-on/wait/toggle-off cycle. All 6 tests PASS. No new tracebacks/exceptions from the new HOD-target-filter, psych-level, or topping-tail code paths found in backend.err.log during or after the test run.

minor.issue: Scan occasionally takes 45-80s (Alpaca REST rate-limiting causes batch retries with backoff), which exceeds the ~60s ingress gateway timeout and returns a 502 to the client even though the backend scan itself completes successfully with no exception (confirmed via backend logs). Pre-existing scanner performance issue, unrelated to this session's auto-trader strategy change - not caused by the HOD/psych/topping-tail code.

minor.endpoint: position_monitor_service (separate from auto_trader_service, monitors the manual ATPC position)
minor.issue: During the toggle-on smoke test window, the pre-existing manual ATPC position's stop-loss trigger fired and failed with an Alpaca 'insufficient qty available (requested 105, available 0, held_for_orders 1)' error - there was a stale/related pending order holding the shares. The position was resolved a moment later ('Position closed, removing from monitor'), so no stuck state resulted, but this is a genuine race-condition-flavored error worth a look. It is NOT part of auto_trader_service.py / the strategy code under test (monitor_exits() never touches ATPC since it isn't in auto_trader.open_positions, as expected) - flagging only because it appeared in logs during this test window.

action_items: No fixes required for the HOD/psych-level/topping-tail strategy logic itself - status defaults correct (reward_risk_ratio=2.0, enable_partial_profit=true, breakeven_buffer_pct=0.2, topping_tail_wick_ratio=0.5), settings round-trip persists correctly for all 3 new fields, entry-conditions endpoint doesn't crash for any tested symbol, and the background auto-trader loop ran through several full scan cycles with the toggle on with zero exceptions traced to the new code paths.

OPTIONAL/OUT-OF-SCOPE FYI: consider investigating the position_monitor_service 'insufficient qty available' error and the scanner's occasional 502-from-slow-scan behavior in a future session, but neither blocks or is related to this strategy change.
critical_code_review_comments: check_entry_signals(): hod_target quality-filter logic (lines 692-700) is correctly gated behind require_micro_pullback and correctly rejects (returns None) when the HOD retest is closer than reward_risk_ratio x risk - matches the spec. psych_target (Target B) computation correctly nulls itself out when it doesn't fall strictly between entry and Target A (line 706).

monitor_exits(): the profit-target ladder (psych first stage -> HOD final stage, with topping_tail as an independent trigger at either stage) is implemented with reasonably clear branching, but the function is now doing a LOT in one method (position updates, topping-tail bar fetch, ladder logic, bailout, trailing stop, exit execution, trade logging) - at ~210 lines for this one method it's a good candidate to split into smaller helpers (e.g. _check_topping_tail, _check_profit_ladder, _execute_exit) for maintainability, though this is a style/maintainability note, not a bug.

auto_trader_service.py file itself is now 1092 lines - exceeds the 700-line guideline; no functional issue found, but worth splitting entry-signal-checking, exit-monitoring, and settings/persistence into separate modules in a future refactor.

_get_real_bars(symbol, '1Min', limit=2) called inside the per-position loop in monitor_exits() only when current_price > entry_price - reasonable guard to avoid unnecessary API calls, and wrapped in try/except so a data-fetch failure degrades gracefully (topping_tail stays False) rather than crashing the exit-monitoring loop - good defensive coding.
seed_data_creation: None - no new data created; all settings changes made during testing (enable_partial_profit, breakeven_buffer_pct, topping_tail_wick_ratio) were restored to their original values (true/0.2/0.5) at the end of each test. Auto-trader toggled ON briefly (~20s) during the toggle smoke test and toggled back OFF afterward - left in OFF state as required.
context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration only covered the new HOD-retest/psych-level/topping-tail auto-trader strategy logic (backend/algorithm-only, no frontend). Iterations 22-23 (sell-anywhere fix, R:R ratio UI, trailing-stop default, Dashboard chart lines) were explicitly out of scope per the request and not retested. Note the pre-existing Trading.js multi-chart 'Loading {symbol}...' stuck-render bug flagged in iteration_23 was NOT retested here (out of scope) and likely still needs RCA if picked up again. The two minor issues logged here (scanner 502-on-slow-scan, position_monitor_service insufficient-qty error) are both unrelated to auto_trader_service.py and did not block any of the required checks.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - no bugs found in the code under test (auto_trader_service.py strategy overhaul + server.py status/settings endpoints). The two minor issues noted are in unrelated pre-existing services (scanner_service's Alpaca rate-limit retry timing vs. gateway timeout, and position_monitor_service's stop-loss execution racing against another pending order) and were only observed incidentally in logs during this test window.
